content:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — elevated 5xx + timeouts for tenant suncrest on dedicated-cluster-7. Trigger: gateway 5xx > 3% (5m), backend timeouts increasing. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/suncrest/cluster-7
Maya R.: Paging oncall. @Jordan (oncall) can you take? :rotating_light:
Jordan (oncall): I'm in, pulling metrics. I see gateway connection queue length ~1200, backend queue drops and a lot of `connection reset by peer`. p99 latency jumping to ~3.2s.
Kevin T.: Adding context — pattern looks like noisy tenant + KV thrash. Backends are hitting high eviction counts, which can stall KV lookups and backpressure the runtime.
Maya R.: Can we confirm KV evictions and pod health? Jordan, run quick checks.
Jordan (oncall): Running now:
```
curl -sS https://gateway.internal/health | jq . 
# {"status":"ok","uptime":"42d"}
redis-cli -h kv-7 INFO memory | grep evicted_keys
# evicted_keys:1423
kubectl get pods -n runtime -l pool=cluster-7 -o wide | grep -E "Pending|CrashLoopBackOff"
```
Jordan (oncall): Redis evictions high, a few model pods pending because GPU allocation failed earlier. Autoscaler did attempt scale up 3m ago.
Priya S.: FYI autoscaler event: `scale-up requested for model-pool-7 -> 3 nodes`, last event 3m ago, status: `pending` due to shortage of nodes in the AZ.
Kevin T.: Quick mitigations proposal: 1) apply per-tenant concurrency cap for suncrest, 2) route a fraction of traffic to fallback cluster-9, 3) evict hot cache shards / reduce cache retention for churny keys.
Maya R.: Agreed. Jordan, apply a soft concurrency limit of 20 for suncrest via admin API. Priya, can we borrow spare GPUs from us-west-2? @ops-bot status?
ops-bot: Spare GPUs in us-west-2: 4 available. Current cluster-9 free capacity: 2 full pods equivalent.
Jordan (oncall): Applying concurrency cap now:
```
POST /admin/tenants/suncrest/config 
{"concurrency_limit":20}
# response: 200 OK
```
Jordan (oncall): Kicked long-running requests with graceful 429s; queue length dropped from ~1200 -> ~340 within 60s. 5xx rate dropping.
Maya R.: Good. Next, let's route 30% traffic to cluster-9 as a quick offload. Priya, please start split rollout.
support-sara: I'll notify Suncrest now that we're performing mitigation which may cause temporary throttling; they'll appreciate a heads-up.
Priya S.: Routing change request sent:
```
POST /routing/tenants/suncrest 
{"split":{"cluster-7":0.7,"cluster-9":0.3}}
```
ops-bot: Routing change accepted, rollout scheduled (canary -> full) starting in 30s.
Jordan (oncall): Monitoring metrics: p50 220ms, p99 640ms, 5xx down to 0.6% after routing. Connection queue decreasing steadily.
Kevin T.: This matches noisy neighbor causing KV pressure. Immediate actions look effective. Long term we should add hot-key detection, per-tenant KV quotas, and auto-shard hot keys. I'll open a follow-up RFC.
Maya R.: Agreed. Also add a follow-up to increase cloud node provisioning limit to avoid pods stuck Pending.
Kevin T.: Creating tickets: INF-4521 (hot-key detection RFC) and INF-4522 (increase provisioning timeout & node pool sizes).
Maya R.: Handoff: Jordan, please monitor for 30 minutes and escalate if 5xx > 1% or queue > 400. I'll stay on for the handoff.
Jordan (oncall): On it — I'll annotate dashboards and leave a short runbook in the incident thread.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Updated: 2287655030
Maya R.: Leaving notes for postmortem: cause = noisy tenant causing high KV evictions -> runtime backpressure -> gateway 5xx/timeouts. Mitigations applied: per-tenant concurrency cap, 30% reroute to cluster-9, cache shard eviction. Next steps: RFCs, infra sizing, customer comms.
support-sara: Sent message to Suncrest support contact: "We've applied temporary throttling while we rebalanced traffic; latency and errors should be improving. We'll follow up with details"
Maya R.: Thanks all — closing for now, will file postmortem if it recurs. :thumbsup:
